newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chip shares close down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chip shares close down on profit-taking.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed sharply lower on Tuesday as investors locked in profits after strong gains in recent trading sessions, dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 15.06 points lower, or 1.22 percent, to 1,220.63.
The small-cap Second Board index was up just 0.35 points to 606.04.
"We expected some profit-taking to come in," said Jonathan Duckett, an institutional dealer at Mohaiyani Securities.
The slide was led by Tenaga which lost 10 cents to 12.80 ringgit and Maybank which fell 75 cents to 26.25 ringgit.

Gaming stocks which made strong gains over the last week took a tumble as prices reached analysts' fair value projections. Magnum lost 20 to 5.10 and Tanjong was down 10 to 11.50. However, Resorts World and Berjaya Leisure both closed in positive territory in late buying
"Gaming stocks are looking pricey again," said Duckett.
"U.S. and U.K. funds have been selling telecommunications stocks in favour of Tenaga," said an institutional dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house. Telekom fell 30 to 20.10.
"There has been some blue-chip buying, but it has been very selective," said the dealer.
